## Disclaimers

- **Preliminary model** — not yet reviewed by clinical staff.
- **Results may shift** until the code is finalized.
- Small cohort; nothing here is externally validated.

## What we did

- Restricted the data to each patient's **first (baseline) observation**.
- Excluded post-treatment variables (based on non-expert review - this is an area where direct collaboration is needed in the future)
- Excluded variables with >90% missing values.
- Predicted using patient-grouped nested cross-validation. Minimal missing data was imputed via fit in-fold only.

## What we saw

- **Prediction holds ~0.70 AUC from baseline data alone.**
- Performance is essentially identical with fuller data — **no late-observation leakage; deployable at intake.**
- **Every prediction comes from pre-treatment variables only** — clean under audit.

## Discrimination

```{python}
#| label: fig-auc
#| fig-cap: "Repeated-CV medians (bars) vs held-out test (diamonds). Frozen receipts from the definitive run."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

models = ["Logistic Regression", "Random Forest", "XGBoost"]
cv_first = [0.683, 0.703, 0.625]
cv_full = [0.685, 0.692, 0.680]
test_first = [0.663, 0.712, 0.607]
test_full = [0.715, 0.645, 0.555]

x, w = np.arange(3), 0.35
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.2))
b1 = ax.bar(x - w / 2, cv_first, w, label="CV median — first look", color="#4C72B0")
b2 = ax.bar(x + w / 2, cv_full, w, label="CV median — full data", color="#9BB7D4")
ax.scatter(x - w / 2, test_first, marker="D", s=26, color="black", zorder=3)
ax.scatter(x + w / 2, test_full, marker="D", s=26, color="black", zorder=3)
ax.scatter([], [], marker="D", s=26, color="black", label="Held-out test")
ax.axhline(0.5, ls="--", lw=0.8, color="grey")
ax.set_xticks(x, models, fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylabel("AUC")
ax.set_ylim(0.45, 0.8)
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8, loc="lower right")
for b in (*b1, *b2):
    ax.text(b.get_x() + b.get_width() / 2, b.get_height() + 0.004,
            f"{b.get_height():.3f}", ha="center", fontsize=7)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
